I have farmed this land my whole life. My father farmed before me, and I learned from him. My 2.2 mu feeds my wife and me, and what's left over I sell at the village market or to the grain station. I don't experiment much — I know what this soil does and what it doesn't do.

**My thinking:**

Same rotation I've done for thirty-plus years: wheat goes in around Cold Dew in October, I harvest it in June, then I get maize in the ground right away on the same field. No sense resting the land when I can run two crops off it.

For wheat, I use the improved variety seeds I buy from the township supply cooperative — the Jimai strain that the local station has been promoting. Hybrid wheat doesn't make sense to me; the improved seed is cheaper and I get good enough yield. I'll do rotary tillage after the maize comes out — the straw I chop and turn in. Before planting I apply base fertilizer: compound fertilizer plus urea. Then at jointing in March I top-dress with urea again. I irrigate three times: once before winter sets in to help the seedlings establish, once at jointing, once at heading. I spray once for weeds in autumn and once for rust and aphids in spring.

For maize, I buy hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or something like it from the co-op, whatever is on offer that year. After wheat harvest I seed directly without plowing, just get it in fast before the heat breaks. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and urea at the big bell stage. Summer rain usually handles most of the water needs, but if July or August is dry I'll pump one more time from the well. One herbicide spray early on, maybe one more if there's pest pressure in late summer.

I'm 62 now. I do what I can myself and my wife helps with seeding and harvesting. We manage.
